defects_repaired.demonstrated_by: tests/test_r1_parser_a_vs_b_cross_validation.py::test_disagreement_conflicting_duplicate_row_order_dependence (pre-repair name; renamed post-repair, see regression_ids below)
defects_repaired.pre_repair_behavior: daily_primitive scanned rows sequentially with a seen_ids dict and silently kept whichever row for a given trdMatchID it encountered first, discarding conflicting rows as 'duplicates' without excluding the retained row from aggregation. close/open/high/low/base_volume/quote_turnover for a day containing a genuinely conflicting duplicate (same trdMatchID, different timestamp/size/price) therefore depended on raw input row order, contradicting the module's own reorder-determinism docstring claim.
defects_repaired.frozen_contract_basis: experiments/data/r1_source_precedence_freeze.json:conflict_rule -- 'Conflicting canonical values ... are fail-closed; no lower-priority source silently replaces a higher-priority fact.'
defects_repaired.repair: daily_primitive now groups all valid rows by trdMatchID before any classification. A group whose members share an identical (timestamp, size, price) is an ordinary exact duplicate (kept once, duplicate_count incremented, DUPLICATE_UNEXPECTED). A group with more than one distinct (timestamp, size, price) is a genuine conflict: every member of that group is excluded from the parsed/aggregated set (added to rejected_row_count) and DUPLICATE_CONFLICTING is raised. Classification depends only on the group's member set, never on which row was physically first, so the result is invariant under any permutation of the input rows.
defects_repaired.policy_choice_source: derived solely from r1_source_precedence_freeze.json:conflict_rule (fail-closed exclusion); no first-row, last-row, average, or other guessed policy was implemented

defects_repaired.demonstrated_by: tests/test_r1_parser_a_vs_b_cross_validation.py::test_disagreement_side_included_in_b_fingerprint_not_in_contract (pre-repair name; renamed post-repair, see regression_ids below)
defects_repaired.pre_repair_behavior: daily_primitive's per-row fingerprint was (timestamp, side, size, price); two rows with identical trdMatchID/timestamp/size/price but differing side were misclassified DUPLICATE_CONFLICTING.
defects_repaired.frozen_contract_basis: unambiguous, not contract-ambiguous: (a) experiments/data/r1_normalized_evidence_contract_v1.json, DailyMarketEvidenceV1.close.duplicate_semantics: 'exact duplicate trade rows (identical trade id/timestamp/price/size) collapse to one observation' -- side is not listed; (b) experiments/data/r1_information_loss_ledger_v1.json field 'side': classification INTENTIONALLY_DISCARDED, reconstruction_rule 'not needed by any of open/high/low/close/base_volume/quote_turnover/trade_count ... side is a taker-direction label, not a price/size/turnover input'.
defects_repaired.repair: canonical trade identity for grouping is trdMatchID alone; the group-distinctness check compares only (timestamp, size, price), matching the frozen contract exactly. side is read from each row (still available for future forensic use) but excluded from both the grouping key and the distinctness check.
